- scripts/review_autofix_step_post_editor_summary.sh:387 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The Python script fetches only `comments(last:100)`, so on a PR with more than 100 comments the newest failure-cap marker can fall outside the fetched window and is not found.
  WHY: On PRs with long discussion threads the script may log `cap_marker_out_of_window` and leave a stale `ai:review-blocked` label, even though the failure marker exists further back (the source severity MAJOR is mapped to high).
- scripts/review_autofix_step_post_editor_summary.sh:345-350 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: A race already existed and the new comment documents it: `fingerprint-cap-block` runs in its own concurrency group and adds the label before posting its cap comment. A cap that lands between this step's GraphQL read (line 372) and its DELETE (line 483) can have its label removed even though that head should stay capped.
  WHY: The label is lost if a concurrent `fingerprint-cap-block` run adds it after the read but before the DELETE, so the head is still capped by marker but no longer has the label (the source severity NIT is mapped to low; the race was already in the original PR and the last run diff only documents it).
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
